title: The Amendments to the International Health Regulations Are Not a Breakthrough
snippet: Those new provisions, however, changed nothing about how the IHR functions. As defined, a pandemic emergency is a PHEIC, and no one has questioned that the PHEIC concept encompasses disease events that were, or could become, pandemics or that the WHO director-general could declare a PHEIC concerning such events. WHO member states did not oppose the director-general's past determinations that certain declared PHEICs were pandemics because such determinations did not affect their obligations [...] The IHR amendments did not adopt a traffic-light approach but instead clarified what was already clear—that the WHO director-general can declare an emergency concerning a disease event that has or could become a pandemic. As with previous determinations that a declared PHEIC was a pandemic, a pandemic emergency declaration does not alter the IHR's PHEIC provisions and processes, enhance the WHO director-general's authority, or create new pandemic-specific obligations for IHR parties. [...] An important revision made to the IHR in 2005 was granting the WHO director-general the authority to declare a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC), even over the objections of the countries directly affected. The PHEIC declaration power applied to disease events that were, or could become, pandemics, as the PHEIC declarations on H1N1 influenza in 2009 and COVID-19 in 2020 illustrate. title: WHO expert: ‘Declaring climate change a global public health emergency would be a turning point’ - Geneva Solutions
snippet:
It would also be crucial in unlocking financing: previous PHEICs that have been called, for example, polio, have seen huge investment off the back of these declarations. So far, we’ve seen pitiful amounts of investment in climate health action, both nationally and internationally, but we hope global financing will step up.

##### All PHEICs to date have been caused by a virus. Is the WHO ready for this paradigm shift? [...] Does climate change fit with the four criteria of a PHEIC?

Climate change is a risk across all health and disease indicators. It’s definitely a cross-border threat. It’s not an epidemic, and it’s not time-bound. So it doesn’t typically fit into the IHR and PHEIC criteria. But then, how else do we sound the alarm? We can’t make the health argument for climate change, for mitigation or for adaptation in other sectors, unless the health sector itself has declared climate change an emergency. [...] Classifying the climate crisis as “public health emergency of international concern” (PHEIC) would encourage greater investment, said Robb Butler, the WHO’s special representative for climate and health at its European regional office. He spoke to Le Temps.

title: WHO Declares Ebola Outbreak in Congo and Uganda a Global Health Emergency
snippet:
More than 300 suspected cases and at least 80 deaths into an accelerating outbreak, the World Health Organization declared the Ebola epidemic spreading across the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) on Sunday, May 17, 2026. The declaration, the most serious alarm WHO can raise short of a pandemic emergency, reflects both the scale of what is already visible and deep uncertainty about how much more may be going undetected in one [...] ### What the Numbers Show — and What They May Be Missing

As of May 16, WHO reported eight laboratory-confirmed cases, 246 suspected cases, and 80 suspected deaths in Ituri Province in eastern DRC, spread across at least three health zones: Bunia, Rwampara, and Mongbwalu. The Africa CDC reported 336 suspected cases and 87 deaths by May 17, and updated figures from the AP placed the total at 88 deaths at the time of the PHEIC declaration. [...] The PHEIC designation is intended to trigger international coordination and resource mobilization. WHO announced it will convene an Emergency Committee as soon as possible to advise on temporary recommendations. Whether the international community can mount a rapid and effective response in an active conflict zone, with no licensed medical tools and a likely undercounted case burden, will define how far this outbreak spreads.
